---
title: "Data browser"
description: >
  Explore spatial gene expression, cell type proportions, ESV scores and PoPS
  disease scores interactively.
---

Select a dataset and a gene to view the spatial expression of that gene beside
the spatial abundance of every cell type. The tables below list the gene's ESV
score for the whole tissue and for each cell type, and its PoPS score for every
trait.

<link href="../databrowser/app.css" rel="stylesheet">

<script src="../databrowser/app.js" defer></script>

## Notes

- **Count** is the raw UMI count for that gene at that spot, exactly as stored in
  the dataset — no normalization or transformation is applied to the numbers you
  see. The *colour* is mapped on a log scale, because raw counts are steep
  enough that a linear ramp would put most spots in the lightest band and hide
  the tissue structure; the colour bar is labelled at its midpoint so the
  non-linearity is visible.
- **Cell type proportion** is the estimated proportion of a cell type at each
  spot; the proportions across all cell types sum to one at every spot. The maps
  are drawn on one common scale so that cell types can be compared with each
  other.
- **ESV** is the expression-based spatial variability score for the gene within
  each cell type, as reported by `spacelink()` and `spacelink_ctSVG()`; `whole`
  is the score across the whole tissue.
- **PoPS** scores come from the Polygenic Priority Score tables and are defined
  per gene and per trait; they do not depend on the dataset or the cell type.
  Traits are listed strongest first. Genes absent from the PoPS tables are
  reported as such.
- Spatial plots are drawn with an equal aspect ratio, with both axes running in
  the same direction as the stored spot coordinates.
